how: Every edit Joel gives goes in here the same turn, with his words and the strings the article must (or must not) contain once it's done. Status pending until the article has it; then applied.
Every note or record that says the article covers something gets a claim entry (for example, which jobs a paragraph explains).

tools/humanization/check_owner_edits.py (from the repo root) checks every entry against the article with comments removed. render_article_so_far.py runs it on every render, and a failure goes in a red box at the top of the article.

A record, note or message says a change is in the article (installed, applied, fixed, resolved, moved, explains) only after its entry passes. If it only exists in a draft, candidate or scratch file, it says so.

entries.where: Love Doesn't Have to Wait for Trust
must_contain: Also notice what else in you answers your little one, besides what you choose to say. When they say "I don't believe you," something in you might fire back an accusation, and then they can learn your love is only there as long as they take it the right way. The resentment can be purely visceral: being doubted after you've tried feels unfair, but there's nothing unfair in them going over your track record. The part that resents not being believed might be the same one that said "I love you" in the first place, or a different one, or a bit of both. Both talk in your grown-up voice, so to your little one they're the same. Be careful not to take the accusation as proof your love really is conditional, when it could just be another part talking.
must_not_contain: the catch is in your love itself
might only be borrowing that voice
the bedtime anger from the other side
nothing to win

entries.where: Love Doesn't Have to Wait for Trust
must_contain: Your little one might not be the only one getting accused. When life has gone badly, part of you may try to get some control back by finding someone to blame, like "If you'd gotten it together at fifteen, you could have saved everybody." If it's somebody's fault, it didn't have to happen, and that feels like control. But figuring out which age of you is to blame doesn't give you what it would have taken back then. That part may start picking on a different age.

must_contain: Whichever age it picks on, saving everybody was never your job. At fifteen you probably didn't even have your own money, or anywhere else to go. And actually, not to beat a dead horse here, but every age of you was stuck with whatever it had then, even the adult you were last year. Hindsight being 20/20 doesn't change that. You still did what you did, though, and if it hurt people or damaged a life, that may need repair.
